biases: Anglophone, US-centric selection: only two China-based voices (Liang Wenfeng, Kai-Fu Lee) and no European or Indian builders.
No women in the builders or investors cohorts and one among researchers (Fei-Fei Li) — a reflection of who held these roles, which also narrows the range of views.
Survivorship: people were selected partly because they became prominent, which favors those whose bets worked.
Claim selection: assertions were chosen as each person's most consequential documented claims; prolific speakers (Altman, Musk, Marcus) have more scorable claims than reticent ones (Sutton, Liang).
Corporate messaging: CEOs' statements often double as marketing; the dataset labels strategic actions separately and never treats an investment as proof of belief.
Hindsight: verdict rationales were written to judge claims on information available at the time, but the analyst knows the outcomes.
limitations: Research ran under a network proxy that blocked direct page fetches, and a shared search quota was exhausted mid-research. About 55% of evidence records are 'unverified recall' and are flagged everywhere; a follow-up verification pass is the top data-quality priority.

117 of 221 assertions are unresolved at the cutoff and 21 more are shown but unscored (self-demonstrated results, investments, advocacy, governance acts), leaving 88 scorable claims. Only 11 of the 30 people clear the ranking threshold (≥3 scorable claims and ≥1.0 total evidential weight); the other 19 are shown as provisional.

Known missing claims flagged by the audit, to add after verification: Marcus's dated 2024/2025 calls, LeCun's 'GPT-5000' remark, Cathie Wood's Tesla robotaxi targets, Musk's power-shortage and Austin robotaxi statements, and other high-profile claims that could shift rankings.
Period 'heat' values and debate 'balance' values are analyst readings of the record, not measured quantities.
2026 developments come from news reporting via search snippets; some figures (lab run-rates, capex) vary by source.
Some 2026 events in this dataset (e.g. model names, the Mythos access order) are reported from search results and could not be cross-checked against primary documents.
periodRevisions: 2012–16 effectively ends with the Transformer (June 2017), not December 2016; kept on calendar years for readability.
2022–23: technical shifts (Chinchilla, InstructGPT, H100, export controls) precede ChatGPT; ChatGPT (Nov 30, 2022) is the break for adoption, capital and policy.
The reasoning era starts with OpenAI o1 (Sept 2024), not January 2025; 2024's snapshot therefore already includes inference-time scaling.
The 2026 period could reasonably start in December 2025 (Gemini 3, credit stress, preemption EO).

audit.finding: Signing the 2023 pause letter (Bengio) was coded as an 'incorrect' action.
audit.action: Reclassified as an aspiration (advocacy); shown but not scored.

audit.finding: Altman's 'novel insights in 2026' was scored correct on contested reports.
audit.action: Confidence lowered to low (halves its weight).

audit.finding: Bootstrap intervals over 3–7 claims looked implausibly tight.
audit.action: Added a small-sample widening term; most top ranks are now reported as ties.

audit.finding: 55% of evidence could not be re-verified against sources.
audit.action: Flagged as 'unverified recall' in every view; evidence-grade filter added to the courtroom; no recalled text shown as a verbatim quote.

audit.finding: Duplicate evidence ids across research batches (outcome sources).
audit.action: Renamed with batch suffixes; all references re-pointed.

audit.finding: Several landmark verdicts admit two readings (Hinton radiology, Marcus 'wall', Amodei 90% code, Chollet on LLMs).
audit.action: Added competing interpretations to each case file.

audit.finding: Musk's last place is robust across all five weightings; the top ranks are not.
audit.action: Leaderboard reports 'no clear winner' when top intervals overlap; sensitivity table shows rank ranges.

audit.finding: [Independent audit f2/f3] The top two ranks (Hassabis, Silver) rested on announcements of their own demonstrated results (AlphaGo counted twice), and Hassabis ranked on an effective weight of 1.45 — below the shrinkage prior.
audit.action: Self-demonstrated results, investments, advocacy and governance acts are now shown but unscored (21 claims); ranking also requires ≥1.0 total evidential weight. Hassabis and Silver move to provisional.

audit.finding: [f1] Hassabis's 'Isomorphic drugs in trials by end-2025' was past its deadline but left unresolved.
audit.action: Resolved incorrect at low confidence (flips if a 2025 first dosing is documented).

audit.finding: [f10/f11] Inconsistent grading: Amodei's 90%-of-code overshoot was partial while comparable misses were incorrect; the power-not-chips claim was graded three ways.
audit.action: Amodei → incorrect (premature); Zuckerberg's power claim → partial, on-time, matching Aschenbrenner's.

audit.finding: [f12–f14, f18] Claims with horizons after the cutoff (Huang 2027, Amodei 2027, Son 2029) or posed as open questions (Gil) carried resolved verdicts.

[f15, f16, f4, f30] Date issues: Hinton's 10-year hedge ends Nov 2026; Liang's GPU purchase was ~2021; Hassabis's AlphaFold claim was dated at its own result; Huang's export-control record bundles three dates.
audit.action: Rationale rewritten; Liang redated to 2021 with originality lowered; AlphaFold claim treated as track record; Huang bundling noted.

audit.finding: [f20–f23] Synthesis overreach: the mechanism-beats-deadline effect largely disappears without Musk; Lee and Son were named for unresolved or absent claims; Sutton praised on two claims; Liang/Aschenbrenner labeled early though coded on-time.
audit.action: Synthesis rewritten to match the data and to separate retained ideas from foresight scores.

audit.finding: [f24–f29] Thesis/debate labels: power-binding and benchmarks-not-intelligence overstated as validated; a contradicting radiology step labeled partial; one debate status inconsistent; two camp placements questionable.
audit.action: Both theses → partial; step → contested; foundation-vs-app → leaning; data camp relabeled; Pichai moved to the build-out camp.
